title: Microlens performance inventory — 6-week snapshot
content:
Purpose: a compact, self-facing inventory of signals and concrete asks to carry into my next 1:1. Use as a microlens (6 weeks) — capture quick wins, unresolved risks, and rehearsal lines.

Context notes:
- Role focus: IC+lead for onboarding ops improvements and early-career coaching. Balancing project delivery (onboarding playbook rollout) and people cadence (triage for new hires).
- Timebox: last 6 weeks (Jan 5 – Feb 15).
- Goal for next 6 weeks: stabilize playbook adoption across 3 pods, reduce onboarding time by 15% for new hires, and seed coaching rituals for 2 managers.

Signals of progress (what I can point to in conversation):
- Adoption: 7 new hires onboarded using v1 playbook; estimated time-to-first-PR dropped from ~9 days to ~7 days (sample n=8).
- Ops throughput: triage queue cleared within 48h for 85% of tickets (baseline was ~62%).
- Coaching: ran 3 manager office hours (avg attendance 6), two managers reported 1:1 structure adoption.
- Feedback: internal survey n=12: net positive feedback on clarity (avg 4.1/5), recurring ask for more role-specific checklists.

Concrete examples / evidence snippets (paste-able into 1:1):
- "Last hire (teammate B): completed first merged PR on day 6 using the playbook checklist — small fixes only. Before playbook, median was day 10."
- "Triage backlog metric: we hit 85% under-48h for the week of Feb 2; I pushed a small routing change that removed a manual handoff (PR-456)."
- "Manager R (backend): adopted weekly 15-min onboarding sync; reports fewer follow-up questions and better clarity on responsibilities."

Behavioral signals I want my manager to notice:
- Proactivity: shipping small infra changes (routing PR) without blocking others.
- Coaching mindset: turning ad-hoc questions into repeatable artifacts rather than answering each time.
- Prioritization tradeoffs: deliberately deprioritized a longer refactor to preserve onboarding momentum.

Current risks / open questions to escalate:
- Capacity risk: if hiring pace doubles next month, current ad-hoc model for role-specific checklists will bottleneck — need a mechanism (templated owners) to scale.
- Measurement noise: sample sizes small; need to instrument first-PR time in analytics to avoid overfitting to anecdata.
- Alignment: product team roadmap includes a new auth flow that will change onboarding steps; need a sync to avoid rework.

Asks for manager (rank-ordered, short):
1) Quick decision: approve hiring contractor (0.5 FTE) to build role-specific checklists for infra + console hires (budget: 6 weeks).
2) Headspace: 30-min sync to align on product auth flow impact and prioritization (blocked items listed below).
3) Sponsor: help introduce the playbook to two senior engineering managers (ask: 15-min intro in their team meeting).
4) Calibration: confirm that reducing time-to-first-PR by ~15% is an acceptable north-star for next quarter (so I can prioritize accordingly).

Rehearsal script (60–90s opener in 1:1):
- "Quick snapshot: the playbook is getting early traction — first-PR time looks like it's improving by ~2 days in our small sample and triage SLAs tightened after the routing fix. The main blocker for scaling is creating role-specific checklists; I’m asking for a short-term contractor to build those so we can onboard at pace without more manager time. Also want to check if you agree on the 15% reduction KPI for next quarter."

Micro-asks & next actions (my TODOs pre-manager meeting):
- Draft contractor brief + scope (2 slides) — due Feb 24.
- Instrument first-PR metric in analytics (event + dashboard) — kickoff with data eng by Feb 28.
- Prepare 1-pager for product auth flow dependencies (highlight 3 steps that change onboarding) — due Feb 25.
- Compile 3 anonymized onboarding stories to share as evidence (B, C, D) — due Feb 24.

Fallbacks if asks are denied:
- If no contractor: recruit a rotational owner from ops (2-week rotation) and reduce scope of checklists to core role tasks only.
- If headspace declines: share a short async doc and ask for a 10-min alignment slot during weekly sync.

Personal coaching goals (6-week experiments):
- Experiment A (habit): run a 15-min onboarding office hour twice weekly and keep attendance notes. Success = >50% re-use of shared artifacts by attendees within 2 weeks.
- Experiment B (skill): practice concise feedback delivery (5-min micro-feedback) during manager syncs; ask manager for a 1-line rating after each.

Self-assessment (quick bullets):
- Wins: shipped routing change, playbook used by 7 hires, started manager office hours.
- Gaps: measurement rigor, need clearer role-specific docs, slower at pushing for budget decisions.
- Stretch: reduce measurement noise by instrumenting events; move from anecdotes to dashboard-driven statements.

Open questions for discussion (for manager):
- Do you prefer contractor hires to be managed by people ops or assigned to a product lead?
- Is the 15% time-to-first-PR reduction an OK target, or should we set a different success metric (CSAT, ramp weeks)?
- How aggressive should I be about deprioritizing the onboarding refactor vs. continuing incremental fixes?

End note (to self): keep this microlens active — review again at mid-March, turn this note into a short async update for the team if we get greenlight on contractor.
